ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=12$, $BC=5$. Point $D$ is outside $\triangle ABC$, and segments $AD$ and $BD$ are drawn. Point $E$ is the midpoint of segment $BD$, $AD=4$, $\angle CAD=\angle CAB$. What is the length of segment $CE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend AD and BC to meet at point F\\
$\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACF=90^\circ=\angle ACB$,\\
Also, $\because$ $\angle CAD=\angle CAB$ and AC=AC,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle AFC$,\\
$\therefore$ AF=AB and BC=CF\\
In $\triangle ABC$, AC=12 and BC=5,\\
$\therefore$ $AB=\sqrt{AC^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=13$\\
$\therefore$ AF=13\\
$\because$ AD=4,\\
$\therefore$ DF=AF−AD=13−4=9\\
$\because$ E is the midpoint of BD,\\
$\therefore$ CE is the midline of $\triangle BDF$\\
$\therefore$ $CE=\frac{1}{2}DF=\boxed{\frac{9}{2}}$

推理：按照指定解析几何方法，取 C=(0,0)，令 AC 为竖直轴，A=(0,12)；令 BC 为水平轴且 B 在左侧，所以 B=(-5,0)。由题意 ∠CAD=∠CAB，且图中 D 在 AC 的另一侧，因此射线 AD 是射线 AB 关于竖直线 AC 的反射。向量 AB = B-A = (-5,-12)，其长度为 sqrt(5^2+12^2)=13，所以反射后的 AD 方向单位向量为 (5,-12)/13。又 AD=4，因此 D=A+4(5,-12)/13=(0,12)+(20/13,-48/13)=(20/13,108/13)。E 是 BD 的中点，所以 E=((-5+20/13)/2,(0+108/13)/2)=(-45/26,54/13)。于是 CE 是从原点 C 到 E 的距离：CE=sqrt((-45/26)^2+(54/13)^2)=sqrt(45^2+108^2)/26=117/26=9/2。

planner_metadata.text_role: Use $AC=12$, $BC=5$, $AD=4$, $E$ midpoint of $BD$, and $\angle CAD=\angle CAB$ to assign coordinates and determine the direction and length of $AD$.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply coordinate geometry: vector reflection across an axis, unit direction vectors, midpoint formula, and distance formula.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=12$, $BC=5$. Point $D$ is outside $\triangle ABC$, and segments $AD$ and $BD$ are drawn. Point $E$ is the midpoint of segment $BD$, $AD=4$, $\angle CAD=\angle CAB$. What is the length of segment $CE$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend AD and BC to meet at point F\\
$\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACF=90^\circ=\angle ACB$,\\
Also, $\because$ $\angle CAD=\angle CAB$ and AC=AC,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle AFC$,\\
$\therefore$ AF=AB and BC=CF\\
In $\triangle ABC$, AC=12 and BC=5,\\
$\therefore$ $AB=\sqrt{AC^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=13$\\
$\therefore$ AF=13\\
$\because$ AD=4,\\
$\therefore$ DF=AF−AD=13−4=9\\
$\because$ E is the midpoint of BD,\\
$\therefore$ CE is the midline of $\triangle BDF$\\
$\therefore$ $CE=\frac{1}{2}DF=\boxed{\frac{9}{2}}$
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure is a geometric figure, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is below and slightly toward the middle, BC is the base direction, and AC and BC form right triangle ABC. D is located outside triangle ABC, on the other side of AC, and AD and BD are drawn; E is marked on BD, located between B and D. According to the layout of the figure, AD can be extended, and BC can be extended to the right, so that the two extension lines meet at point F.

Then reason: Because CF and CB are collinear, and the problem gives ∠ACB=90°, ∠ACF=90°=∠ACB. Also because F is on the extension of AD, ∠CAF=∠CAD; the problem gives ∠CAD=∠CAB, therefore ∠CAF=∠CAB. Adding that AC is a common side, △ABC and △AFC are congruent by ASA. From congruence, AF=AB and CF=BC.
In right triangle ABC, AC=12 and BC=5, so AB=sqrt(12^2+5^2)=sqrt(169)=13. Therefore AF=13. Also AD=4, and D is on AF, so DF=AF-AD=13-4=9.
Because CF=BC, and B, C, F are collinear, C is the midpoint of BF. The problem states that E is the midpoint of BD. In triangle BDF, C and E are respectively the midpoints of BF and BD, therefore CE is the midline of triangle BDF, CE=1/2 DF=1/2×9=9/2.
